result.key: BASELINE: broad geography / maps / earth facts (where Myth Juice is now)
result.sharpened_definition: The sharpest honest version of the broad niche: "True stories about places on the real map, shown on a photoreal 3D Earth: what is really there, what is hidden under the water and ice, and what the map has been getting wrong." It is still a broad promise, and Geography By Geoff, RealLifeLore, Atlas Pro and Map Pack already make it at scale.
result.demand:
Demand is very high. A broad-geography channel is not short of audience.

**What was measured**
- 54 YouTube search probes, all on 2026-11-08. 48 were broad probes; each pulled 4 result sets (relevance, this-year relevance, this-year 4-20 min sorted by views, this-year 20+ min sorted by views). 6 more targeted the myth, drain and true-size angles.
- 2,454 unique videos. After keeping English, long-form (6 min or more), under 12 months old and on-niche (hand-curated by channel and keyword; travel vlogs, news, gaming, paranormal and Indian exam prep removed): **332 videos, 266 of them with 100K+ views, from 150 distinct channels.**
- The median captured on-niche recent long-form had 383K views. That figure is inflated because search surfaces winners.

**Biggest recent videos in the sample**
- Geography By Geoff, "Why Almost NOBODY Lives On Australia's West Coast": 10.4M, 1 month old.
- Cleo Abram, "What's Hidden Under Antarctica?": 10.8M, 5 months.
- Geoff, "Why 60,000 People Live on a Rock with Zero Resources": 7.76M, 5 months.
- Epic Adventure Archives, "Drake Passage": 7.0M, 7 months.
- Mr. Science, "When Antarctica Was a Jungle": 5.37M, 2 months.
- Uncharted Depths, "Mariana Trench: What They Found...": 4.1M, 8 months.
- Geoff, "...Africa's Coast": 3.83M, 3 months.
- RealLifeLore, "What's Hidden Under the Jungles of New Guinea?": 2.56M, 10 months.
- RealLifeLore, "Why 'Nobody' Lives on the Pacific Northwest Coast": 795K in 7 days.
- Unseen Works, "What Antarctica Looks Like Without Ice": 1.75M, 3 weeks.

**Top channels keep paying out**
- Geoff's last 30 uploads have a median of 652K. The newest four had 411K at 2 days, 172K at 4 days, 233K at 9 days and 673K at 11 days.
- RealLifeLore's last 30 have a median of 1.15M.

**Demand by sub-format** (100K+ videos in the sample)
- Other place/earth explainers: 58
- "X Is Hiding Something Nobody Talks About": 41
- Deep ocean / trench: 30
- Maps / borders / true size: 26
- Deep time / paleo: 20
- N-facts lists: 18
- Forbidden / unreachable places: 18
- "Why nobody lives here": 17
- Drain / without water or ice / sea-level what-ifs: 17

**Search keywords** (vidIQ data from context.md)
- Rising: "tristan da cunha" ~315K/mo (+118%), "underwater archaeology discoveries" 168K (+185%), "what would happen if" 217K (+134%), "how long would you survive in every era of earth" (+6,464%).
- Most single premises, though, have close to zero search volume. Ep01 got 9 search impressions. This niche lives on Suggested and Browse.

**Angle checks**
- "geography myths everyone believes" and "geography misconceptions": only 6 recent 100K+ long-forms each, from 5 channels (Map Pack 271K and 131K, The Infographics Show 214K in 4 days, Price of Travel 702K).
- The myth framing on its own is a thin demand pocket, much smaller than reveal or place-story premises.

result.competition:
Competition is very crowded at the channel level and gets cloned quickly at the format level.

**Who competes**
- 150 distinct channels had at least one on-niche English long-form above 100K in the last 12 months, and that is only what 48 probes surfaced.
- Sizes (current subscriber counts, read from the channel pages):
  - 1M+ subs: 28 channels, 74 of the 266 hits.
  - 100K-1M: 29 channels, 58 hits.
  - 10K-100K: 52 channels, 91 hits.
  - Under 10K: 30 channels, 32 hits.
  - 11 hits were credited to collab channels whose size could not be resolved.

**The quality bar at the top is high and the top channels upload often**
| Channel | Subs | Median of last 30 long-forms | Uploads |
|---|---|---|---|
| Geography By Geoff | 1.13M | 652K | ~10/month |
| RealLifeLore | 7.93M | 1.15M | |
| Spotniks | 2.25M | 1.15M | |
| Astrum Earth | 504K | 1.2M | |
| Joe Scott | 2.56M | 647K | |
| ExtinctZoo | 1.55M | 636K | |
| PBS Eons | 3.22M | 478K | |
| Atlas Pro | 1.28M | 351K | |
| Bixu | 3.16M | 749K | |
| The Paint Explainer | 2.02M | 518K | |

Map Pack (443K) and Coggnize (547K) run the facts-list format.

**Mass-produced or low-effort channels**
- 46 of the 139 resolved channels match strict signatures:
  - templated title families in 30% or more of uploads;
  - 15 or more uploads a month on a channel under 100K subs;
  - 30% or more of uploads being 90-minute-plus sleep or compilation videos.
- Among the 82 sub-100K channels with a hit, 43 (52%) match. About 10 more look like farms: a median upload under 1K views plus one 300-3,000x outlier (World Untangled, Deep Life Science, Vault of Discovery, HiddenHistory-02, El Archivo Secreto, World Cracked, Rabbit Hole Facts and others). That makes roughly 60-65% of the small-channel winners low-effort.

**Templates get flooded**
- "X Is Hiding Something Nobody Talks About": **34 channels, 210 uploads in 12 months** among the channels I scanned. Median 17,500 views; 55 passed 100K.
- "We Drained X. Here's What Was Hidden": Contour Atlas, The Hidden Provinces, Bright Side Dark Secrets, HiddenHistoryForSleep, plus a Korean channel at 966K. The drain / without-water / sea-level what-if cluster has 17 hits from 15 channels, and 10 of them came in the last 90 days, so it is spreading fast.

**Why the farms matter**
Their hits often rest on sensational or false hooks: "What NASA Actually Found At The Bottom Of The Ocean", Tartaria, the ice wall. The owner's no-false-claims rule forbids those hooks, so Myth Juice cannot match the farms' click-bait. It has to win on retention.

topic_depth: Lake Powell drained: the Glen Canyon hidden under the reservoir, rendered from the USGS 1959 pre-dam terrain (already on file as an ep03 candidate).
The Mediterranean that dried up: the Messinian salinity crisis (about 5.96-5.33 million years ago) and the Zanclean refill through Gibraltar.
Doggerland: the drowned country between Britain and Europe, and the Storegga slide tsunami about 8,200 years ago.
Beringia: the Ice Age land bridge from Siberia to Alaska, exposed when sea level was about 120 m lower.
The Missoula Floods: Ice Age megafloods that scoured Washington's Channeled Scablands, and J Harlen Bretz, mocked for decades and then proven right.
Lake Bonneville: Utah's vanished Ice Age lake and the Bonneville Flood through Red Rock Pass about 14,500 years ago; the Great Salt Lake is what is left.
Africa vs Greenland at true size: Africa is about 14 times larger (30.4M vs 2.17M km2), though they look similar on a Mercator map.
What is under Greenland's ice: drain the ice sheet and the interior is a bedrock bowl near or below sea level.
Camp Century: the US Army's nuclear-powered base inside the Greenland ice (1959-1967), and the frozen soil from it that showed Greenland was ice-free about 400,000 years ago.
Point Nemo: the spot farthest from any land (about 2,688 km), where old spacecraft are sunk; the nearest people are often the astronauts overhead.
Tristan da Cunha (rising keyword): the most remote inhabited island, whose 1961 eruption sent the entire population to England, and why most went back in 1963.
Bouvet Island: the most remote island on Earth and the abandoned lifeboat found on it in 1964.
Surtsey: the island born from the sea off Iceland in 1963 and kept off-limits to everyone but scientists.
Anak Krakatau 2018: the 'child of Krakatoa' whose flank collapsed into the sea and set off a deadly night-time tsunami.
The Salton Sea: California's accidental lake, made in 1905-1907 when the Colorado River broke through an irrigation canal.
The Aral Sea: how one of the world's four largest lakes lost about 90% of its water and left ships stranded in the desert at Moynaq.
Point Roberts, Washington: the US town you can reach by land only by driving through Canada.
The Darien Gap: the one break in the Pan-American Highway between Alaska and Argentina.
Old River Control: the Mississippi 'wants' to jump to the Atchafalaya, and the Army Corps has held it back since 1963.
Lake Nyos 1986: the Cameroon lake that released a carbon dioxide cloud and killed about 1,746 people in one night.
Yellowstone at true size: the caldera (about 45 x 85 km) laid over US cities, and the Huckleberry Ridge eruption 2.1 million years ago.
Chicxulub: the dinosaur-killing crater buried under Yucatan, traced on the surface by a ring of cenotes.
Zealandia: the drowned continent, about 94% underwater, argued to be a continent in 2017.
Lake Baikal drained: the deepest lake on Earth (1,642 m) holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water in a splitting rift.
Everest's summit is seafloor: the top of the world is marine limestone full of fossils from an ancient ocean.
result.engine_fit:
The engine fits only part of the niche, about 6 out of 10.

**Clusters where the engine is a real advantage.** These are the reveal formats where real terrain and seafloor beat the farms' generated stills and stock footage:
- drain / without water or ice: 17 hits
- deep ocean / trenches: 30
- deep time / paleo-geography: 20
- Antarctica: 9
- mountains: 12
- forbidden or remote places reached by flyover: 18

Together that is **106 of 266, or 40% of the 100K+ demand**. True-size overlays add the maps/true-size cluster (26).

**Clusters where it adds little.** About half the volume is formats that run on a 2D map plus drone or stock footage:
- "Is Hiding Something" regional videos: 41
- N-facts lists: 18
- "Why nobody lives here" explainers: 17
- many of the 58 general place explainers

There, Geoff, Coggnize and the template farms win on research volume and upload speed (10-30 a month), not visuals. Myth Juice cannot match that pace or the presenter research.

**Conclusion.** Staying broad wastes the engine on formats where it gives no edge. Its edge appears only when the premise is a spatial reveal, which ep01's one praised shot and the 1.8M Antarctica outlier both confirm.
result.brand_fit:
Brand fit is moderate, about 5 out of 10.

**What fits**
- "Myth Juice" promises myth-busting with flavour.
- The broad niche matches the owner's rules: storytelling, true stories, few big numbers, no on-screen sources.
- The owner's no-false-claims rule is a real point of difference against the farms, whose hits often rest on false hooks ("What NASA Actually Found...", "ice wall", Tartaria).

**What does not**
- Broad geography gives viewers no reason to subscribe to Myth Juice instead of Geoff, RealLifeLore or Map Pack. Ep01 gained +0 subs.
- The "myth" half of the brand has little demand on its own. The geography myth and misconception probes found only about 6 recent 100K+ long-forms from 5 channels; Map Pack's "50 Geography Facts That Are Fake" did 2.95M over a year.
- So the name fits best as a frame: "the map you know is lying / what is really under it". Myth-busting as the main format fits less well.

Phrases that fit the name and the engine: "what's really under it" and "the map is lying". A list of myths does not.
result.monetization:
**RPM**
- Education & Science is the best-paying broad category in third-party data. AIR Media-Tech's 300-channel 2026 dataset gives a median RPM of $10.22 (bottom quartile about $2.31, top about $19.50) and 77% of views monetized.
- Guides put geography and documentary at roughly $4-14 RPM.
- These are third-party estimates; YouTube publishes no niche RPMs.

**Audience geography is the main risk to RPM**
- A broad "geography" audience skews heavily toward South Asia. Many probe results were Hindi or Indian exam-prep geography (UPSC, Study Boost Hindi, Dhruv Rathee at 8-22M views).
- US-framed topics skew to high-RPM viewers. Ep01 had 28% US views but 43% of watch time.
- Practical rule: frame topics around US and UK places and use feet and miles to pull the RPM toward the top of the range.

**Advertisers and format**
- Very advertiser-friendly: evergreen, family-safe, educational.
- Disaster stories need tasteful handling.
- 12-15 minute films allow mid-rolls.
- Sleep-doc and compilation formats earn long watch time but lower RPM and look like farms.

**Policy**
YouTube's "inauthentic content" rule (renamed in July 2025) targets mass-produced, templated videos. That threatens the farm competitors' monetization, and it rewards a channel with original scripts and visuals, as long as Myth Juice's own titles and formats never look templated.
result.risks:
1. **No defensible identity.** In the broad niche Myth Juice is video number 151 next to 28 channels with 1M+ subs. Viewers arrive one video at a time from Suggested and do not subscribe (ep01 +0). The channel stays a lottery ticket per upload.
2. **Templates get cloned.** Any format that works is copied within weeks:
   - "Hiding Something": 34 channels, 210 uploads in 12 months.
   - Drain: 10 of 17 hits came in the last 90 days, from 15 channels.
   The drain race already threatens ep02.
3. **Small-channel hits are mostly farm lottery wins.** Small channels median 1.3K views per upload under 10K subs and 12K at 10-100K, and that is among survivors. Reaching the owner's 1M goal needs a premise-level outlier, not just being in the niche.
4. **Honesty caps clicks.** The owner's no-false-claims rule rules out the sensational hooks that many farm breakouts used, so the CTR edge has to come from imagery: real terrain and seafloor reveals.
5. **The engine is wasted on half the demand.** Lists and regional explainers win on research speed, not visuals.
6. **Myth demand is thin.** Pure geography-myth content is a small pocket, so the brand promise and the demand do not line up unless myths are reframed as "what's really under the map".
7. **Search is close to zero for most premises.** Everything depends on CTR in the Suggested feed next to giant hosts.
8. **Policy risk.** The July 2025 "inauthentic content" rule could hit Myth Juice too if its titles or formats start to look templated.
9. **Measurement caveats.**
   - The sample is search-surfaced, so it is biased toward winners.
   - Subscriber counts are current, after the breakouts.
   - Mass-production flags are heuristics: watch pages returned HTTP 429, so YouTube's own synthetic-content labels could not be read.
result.scores:
- Demand: 10. 266 recent 100K+ long-forms from 150 channels in 48 probes; hits of 5-10M within months.
- Low competition: 2. 28 channels with 1M+ subs uploading monthly; 34 channels on one title template; drain clones spreading.
- Small-channel breakout rate: 7. 46% of 100K+ hits come from channels under 100K subs, and channels with 1.4-5K subs reach 0.2-2.4M. But the median upload on small channels is only 1.3-12K, and about 60% of the small winners look like farms.
- Topic depth: 10. Effectively unlimited.
- Engine fit: 6. The engine is an advantage in about 40% of the demand (reveal, paleo and ocean formats) and irrelevant in the rest.
- Brand fit: 5. It fits the earth-stories half of the name; the myth half has thin demand.
- Defensibility: 2. No unique promise against Geoff, RealLifeLore and Map Pack, and the farms clone any format within weeks.

Verdict: the broad niche is saturated as a channel position but not closed to single videos. The data says to keep the audience pool but narrow the channel's promise to engine-native reveal formats.

result.landscape:
SHORT ANSWER, FROM THE DATA: The niche as a whole is NOT saturated. Drained-ocean / without-ice videos are a narrower slice of it, and that slice is filling up right now. Narrowing the TOPIC further is not supported by the data. Narrowing the FORMAT (one signature format, at low volume) is.

SCOPE
- 99 YouTube search probes (1,606 unique videos; filters: last 12 months, sorted by views, plus relevance mode).
- 155 channel pages fetched for subscriber counts and their last ~30 uploads.
- 3 vidIQ calls (15 credits).
- Caveats: search returns the top 20 per query, so this is a sample, not a census. Subscriber counts are today's (after any breakout). Views on uploads under 3 days old are not settled.

1) Overall niche (English faceless maps / geography / earth, long-form 6 min+)
- 134 videos with 100K+ views in the last 12 months, from 82 distinct channels.
- Hits by channel size today:
  - 1M+ subs: 17 channels, 43 hits
  - 100K-1M: 22 channels, 33 hits
  - 10-100K: 28 channels, 41 hits
  - under 10K: 14 channels, 16 hits (12%). 11 of those 16 are "what is at the bottom / beneath / without water" spectacle.
- 23 of the 82 hit-making channels (28%) upload 20+ long videos a month (mass production).
- Demand at the top is healthy:
  - RealLifeLore: median recent upload 1.3M (older 1.0M).
  - Geography By Geoff: median 726K, one video at 10M (Australia's west coast, 1 month old).
  - Astrum Earth: 504K subs, median 1.45M (2.9 views per subscriber).
  - Mr. Science (deep time): 266K subs, median about 2.1M.
  - Decliners: What If (275K, down from 587K), PolyMatter (187K, from 326K), Map Pack (24K on 443K subs) and Signore Galilei (3.2K, from 107K). The audience is moving from map trivia and geopolitics talk toward visual earth-science spectacle and deep time, which is Myth Juice's engine.

2) The flood is at the bottom, and it is one-hit
- Across 93 sub-100K channels in this niche, the median channel's typical recent upload (7-90 days old) gets about 2,000-3,500 views:
  - Low-volume channels (under 20 uploads a month): median 1,950; top quartile 30,750+.
  - Mass-volume channels: median 3,500; top quartile about 9,700.
- The famous small-channel outliers in context.md are mostly lottery tickets on otherwise dead channels:
  - Unseen Works: Antarctica 1.75M; its other videos 1.2K-2.7K.
  - Contour Atlas: drains 110-170K; its non-drain videos 145-1,600.
  - Below The Map: 442K, then 362-980.
  - Unknown America: 313K, then 286-1,400.
  - Map Redacted: 473K, then 169-2,600.

3) The drain / without-water micro-niche (ep02's lane)
- 96 uploads from 50 channels in about 35 days, 25 of them in the last 3 days.
- For the 71 uploads aged 3+ days: median 448 views; 63% under 2K; 15% over 100K. The hits are concentrated in the first movers.
- Hawaii-specific: 2 brand-new Hawaii drain uploads appeared in the last 12 hours, after the brief's probe:
  - "What Happens If You Drain The Pacific Around Hawaii?: Mauna Kea Measured From..." (Shape Of America, 2 views)
  - "Draining the Pacific Ocean: Hawaii, Zealandia and the Mariana Trench Revealed (4K)" (WATERLINE, 79 subs, 1 view)
  - This is on top of Bright Side Dark Secrets' 9K sleep doc.

4) Where small channels hold a real baseline (not one hit)
These channels have one signature format and post 1-10 videos a month:
- Paintify: 22K subs, 13 videos, median 345K ("Every X" painted maps)
- Fossil: 54K, 15 videos, median 487K ("How long you'd last in every prehistoric X")
- Xverse: 77K, median 538K (3D scale reveals)
- The Last Day: 35K, 24 videos, median 144K (3D Earth what-ifs)
- Curiosity Dude: 38K, median 99K (remote islands, 20-25 min)
- Where They Stood: 3.5K subs, 10 videos, median 30K, top video 4.4M (true stories of places you can't visit)
- Earthyphus: 1.5K subs, 8 videos, median 40K
Topic-narrow channels do worse: drains only (Contour Atlas 690, Drained Atlas 7.8K, Waterline Atlas 46) or one region only (Northern Grounds 1.1K, Map Redacted 1,950).

IMPLICATION
Keep the broad Earth / place topic space. Own one recognizable format: a photoreal 3D real-Earth reveal plus a true story with a single named place and a US anchor.
- The healthiest lanes in the data are deep time on real places and true place stories:
  - Deep time: 15 channels, no single owner, median channel recent upload about 187K, only 3 mass producers.
  - True place stories: Where They Stood; Curiosity Dude.
- For ep02: ship fast, and do not let packaging read as clone number 51.
  - "We Drained..." titles now median 448 views; at least 14 channels use the exact "We Drained X. Here's What Was Hidden at the Bottom." wording.
  - Lead with the Hawaii-specific true-height story, not the drain verb.

Median channel recent upload: 17K. Dozens of near-identical 'Mariana Trench: What They Found in the Deepest Place on Earth' titles.

AI SLEEP DOCS / 1-4 HOUR EARTH DOCUMENTARIES: Just About Earth (65.6K subs, 365 long videos a year, recent uploads 1.8K-6.7K), Bright Side Dark Secrets (43.8K subs, 1,600 videos, median 1.8K), Science for Sleep (274 a year), Project Nightwatch (225 a year), Deep Past Earth (59 videos in 2 months, median 181). High volume, low views per video.

GENERIC 'GEOGRAPHY EXPLAINED / WHY NOBODY LIVES HERE' (the head of the niche): owned by incumbents. 43 hits in the sample from 18 channels: 27 from channels with 1M+ subs (Geography By Geoff alone about 20), 11 from 100K-1M, 5 from 10-100K, 0 from under 10K. Geoff posts 18 videos a month at a 726K median. Hard for a new channel to enter head-on.

TRUE SIZE / MERCATOR: a one-off news spike (the UN map vote, Sep-Oct 2026) captured by BBC, France24, DW, Indian exam-prep channels and World Maps Online (789K and 274K). The channel's next videos fell back to 3.4K-29K.
breakout_patterns: FIRST MOVER ON A NEW VISUAL PREMISE WINS; COPIES DO NOT. Unseen Works' Antarctica Without Ice: 1.75M on 2.9K subs (773x the channel's typical views). Its 9 copies got 33K at best, and most got under 2K. Contour Atlas's first 'We Drained' videos got 165K and 170K on 1.4K subs; 30+ clones followed, median under 1K. The window looks like about 2 weeks before the feed fills up.

THE FORMAT PULLS VIEWS, NOT THE CHANNEL. Small breakout channels do not keep an audience. Unseen Works' non-drain videos got 1.2K-2.7K; Contour Atlas's non-drain videos 145-1,600; Earth Tipping's median is 2,850 after its 961K hit; Below The Map got 362-980 after 442K; Unknown America 286-1.4K after 313K; Super Freaky Science 150-1,100 around its 219K hit; Documentary Overload 575-4.8K after 704K. Of the niche's 100K+ hits from the last year, 16 of 134 came from channels still under 10K subs; 11 of those 16 are spectacle (bottom / beneath / without water).

result.sharpened_definition: Take the water, ice or rock away from one famous place, on real survey terrain, so viewers can see the one thing everybody gets wrong about it, then tell the true human story the reveal uncovers (e.g. "Hawaii Is Only the Tip. We Drained the Ocean."). This is a myth-busting reveal show, not another "We Drained X. Here's What Was Hidden at the Bottom." inventory.

topic_depth: Crater Lake drained: America's deepest lake (1,943 ft) is the collapsed top of Mount Mazama (about 7,700 years ago). The drain shows the hidden Merriam Cone, and the 'Old Man of the Lake' log has floated upright since at least 1896.
Niagara turned off: from June to November 1969 the US Army Corps of Engineers really dewatered the American Falls to inspect the rock. A real drain, with public-domain photos.
Tulare Lake: once the largest freshwater lake west of the Mississippi, drained for farmland, and back in the 2023 floods.
Owens Lake: Los Angeles' 1913 aqueduct drained it, and the dry bed became the single largest source of dust pollution in the US.
Lake Mead lowered: St. Thomas, a Nevada town founded in 1865 and drowned behind Hoover Dam, walks back out of the water in droughts.
Glacial Lake Missoula: an ice-dammed lake that emptied catastrophically again and again, carving the Channeled Scablands. J Harlen Bretz was ridiculed for saying so in 1923 and was proved right.
Lake Bonneville: Salt Lake City sits on the floor of an Ice Age lake about the size of Lake Michigan, which burst out through Red Rock Pass in the Bonneville Flood.
Puget Sound drained: a glacier-carved trough, with the wreck of 'Galloping Gertie' (the 1940 Tacoma Narrows Bridge) still lying on the bottom.
Monterey Canyon: drain the sea off California and a submarine canyon comparable in depth to the Grand Canyon appears.
Hudson Canyon: the Hudson River's drowned Ice Age valley runs across the shelf to a giant canyon about 100 miles off New York City.
Florida was twice as big: lower the Gulf about 400 ft and find Page-Ladson in the Aucilla River, where a mastodon tusk was cut by people about 14,550 years ago.
Beringia drained: a land bridge up to about 1,000 km wide between Siberia and Alaska, with Big and Little Diomede 2.4 miles apart across the date line.
Long Island and Cape Cod without the sea: both are moraines, rubble piles dumped by the last ice sheet.
The whale in Vermont: a beluga skeleton dug up in Charlotte, Vermont, in 1849, left behind by the Ice Age Champlain Sea.
Yellowstone Lake drained: hydrothermal vents and Mary Bay, the largest known hydrothermal-explosion crater (about 13,000 years old), on the lake floor.

Bermuda Triangle drained (myth-bust): Bermuda's volcanic pedestal and the Puerto Rico Trench (about 8,400 m, the Atlantic's deepest). The US Coast Guard does not treat the 'Triangle' as a special hazard area.
Mariana Trench drained: Challenger Deep, about 36,000 ft. Everest would vanish with more than a mile to spare. Trieste's 1960 dive is the human beat.
Zealandia: drain the southwest Pacific to raise Earth's hidden continent, about 94% under water, formally argued as a continent in 2017.
Antarctica's Gamburtsev Mountains: strip the ice from an Alps-sized range no human has ever seen (Antarctica itself is saturated, so it needs this specific angle).
Camp Century: peel back Greenland's ice to the US Army's nuclear-powered under-ice base (1959-67) and the 31-km Hiawatha impact crater (warning: Greenland drains are 0 for 5 for small channels).
Kara-Bogaz-Gol: in 1980 the Soviet Union dammed this Caspian gulf, it dried to a salt flat within about three years, and the dam came down in 1992.
The day Britain became an island: drain the Strait of Dover to show the giant scour valleys cut when a dammed ice-age lake overflowed (first breach about 450,000 years ago, Gupta et al.).
Chicxulub: drain the Gulf of Mexico and strip the limestone to reveal the buried crater, about 180 km wide, of the asteroid that ended the dinosaurs.
Lake Baikal drained: the world's deepest lake (1,642 m) sits in a rift holding up to about 7 km of sediment.
Sundaland: lower the sea about 120 m and Borneo, Sumatra and Java join Asia as one Ice Age landmass (small-channel proof: 272K on 2.2K subs).

10/10 technically. Our engine renders this natively:
- ETOPO/GEBCO/SRTM DEM terrain and seafloor
- an animated water plane, so drain shots are a parameter change
- GPlates paleo-coastlines
- true-size overlays, cut-aways and NASA GIBS imagery

Every idea in the list is a DEM job, with no stock footage. The CC0 characters on the drained floor provide gags (C11). The engine also enforces honesty: the reveal is real bathymetry, which the clones (stock and AI imagery, invented "hidden" objects) cannot match.

Caveat backed by data: the engine alone is NOT an edge. WATERLINE (79 subs) publishes real-terrain 4K drains and gets 1-25K views, and The Vanishing Map does story-led drains at 8-121 views. Our engine converts only with the packaging and story levers below.

How to stand out (from the data):
1. Be first on a famous subject nobody has drained, and check the day before upload. Every breakout above was a first; copycats got 0.01-2% of the original.
2. Use a title grammar different from the clone template (35-50 characters, a claim or myth-bust): "Hawaii Is Only the Tip." works; "We Drained X. Here's What Was Hidden" is fatigued and now policy-risky.
3. Run 12-14 minutes against the clones' 20-30 (our target_length rule).
4. Build one true human spine plus one unspent payoff number, not a list of finds.
5. Open a "really drained" sub-lane (Niagara 1969, Owens, Tulare, Missoula, Kara-Bogaz-Gol) that pure simulators cannot copy.
6. Cut 1-2 drain Shorts per film (the drain Shorts above reached 10-31M views).
7. Keep one signature device across episodes, such as a depth gauge or waterline counter, so the series is recognisable without becoming a template.
result.brand_fit:
7/10.

Where it fits: "Myth Juice" is myth-busting and true stories about places. A reveal fits perfectly when the removal disproves a belief:
- Hawaii is only the tip.
- Florida was twice as big.
- The Bermuda Triangle is ordinary seafloor.
- Salt Lake City sits on a lake bed.
- Niagara has been switched off before.

Where it misfits: a pure drain channel is not a myth channel, and would make Myth Juice look like clone #34.

Owner rules:
- "No false claims" is hard to keep in this format, because clones win clicks with invented "what was hidden" items. We must keep payoffs real, which needs stronger packaging and real stories to compensate.
- "Only a few big vivid numbers" is at risk too: drains invite depth counters on every shot, so cap them at 5 per film.
- No-emoji, no-AI-mention and description-only-sources are all compatible.
- One visual language is natural, since the whole film is photoreal DEM.

Recommended framing: the reveal is Myth Juice's signature DEVICE inside the true-place-stories promise, not the whole channel identity.
result.monetization:
Good. US-place subjects pull a US- and Canada-heavy audience. The best small-channel hits were the Great Lakes, Chesapeake, Tahoe and Lake Ontario, and US viewers watched about 1.9x longer than everyone else on ep01. Global subjects (Antarctica, Pacific, Sundaland) pull lower-RPM worldwide audiences.

RPM benchmarks (third-party trackers; YouTube publishes no official niche figures):
- Education/Science median RPM about $10.22, with the middle half at $2.31-19.50 (AIR Media-Tech, 300 channels).
- US education channels: about $8-18.
- History/documentary: about $6-14, typical US about $9.
- Plan on about $8-10 RPM for US-anchored episodes.

Advertiser safety: very safe (geology and water, nothing graphic), with three cautions:
- treat war wrecks as war graves (Midway, Galloping Gertie is fine);
- no "bodies in barrels" Lake Mead framing;
- no disaster hype.

Running 12-14 minutes allows mid-rolls.

Policy note: YouTube's July 2025 "inauthentic content" clarification targets mass-produced, near-duplicate template videos. The "We Drained X. Here's What Was Hidden" clone channels are exactly that profile. Myth Juice must vary structure, story and visuals per episode, or it risks a YPP review problem when it applies.
